# Model and source

```{r meta}
mod <- readModelDb("Purwonugroho_2012_vancomycin")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Description: `r ui$description`
* Article (DOI): <https://doi.org/10.1100/2012/762649>

Purwonugroho et al. (2012) developed the first population PK model of
vancomycin in Thai adults from routine therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM)
samples. The final model is a two-compartment model in which clearance is
proportional to Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance and the central volume is
proportional to age:

* `CL (L/h) = 0.044 * CLCr (mL/min)`
* `V1 (L) = 0.542 * Age (years)`
* `Q = 6.95 L/h`, `V2 = 44.2 L`

# Population

The analysis used retrospective TDM data from adults (> 18 years) in any ward
of Ramathibodi Hospital, Mahidol University, Bangkok, Thailand, between
January 2007 and June 2010. Patients were randomised into a modeling group and
a validation group. The final modeling group had 212 patients with 391 serum
concentrations (1.84 per patient, range 1-8); the validation group had 34
patients with 68 concentrations (Table 1). In the modeling group the mean age
was 66.62 +/- 18.38 years, mean weight 57.64 +/- 11.62 kg, 47.17% were female,
mean serum creatinine 3.12 +/- 2.92 mg/dL and mean Cockcroft-Gault creatinine
clearance 35.07 +/- 29.83 mL/min. About one third of the patients were in an
ICU and 34.43% were on dialysis (Discussion). Dosing regimens varied between
and within patients. Serum vancomycin was measured by fluorescence
polarisation immunoassay (Axsym; limit 2.00 mg/L). The model was fit in
NONMEM VII (ADVAN3 TRANS4).

```{r population}
str(ui$population)
```

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL slope on CRCL) | `log(0.044)` L/h per mL/min | Table 2, theta1 (CL = theta1 x CLCr) |
| `lvc` (V1 slope on AGE) | `log(0.542)` L/year | Table 2, theta2 (V1 = theta2 x Age) |
| `lq` | `log(6.95)` L/h | Table 2, theta3 |
| `lvp` | `log(44.2)` L | Table 2, theta4 |
| `etalcl` | `0.3578^2 = 0.128` | Table 2, omega CL = 35.78% |
| `etalvc` | `0.2093^2 = 0.0438` | Table 2, omega V1 = 20.93% |
| `etalq` | `0.3950^2 = 0.156` | Table 2, omega Q = 39.50% |
| `etalvp` | `0.5727^2 = 0.328` | Table 2, omega V2 = 57.27% |
| `addSd` | 4.51 mg/L | Table 2, sigma (additive intraindividual variability) |
| Two-compartment structure, first-order elimination | n/a | Methods 2.1 (ADVAN3 TRANS4); Results (two- vs one-compartment dOFV 154.346) |
| Proportional IIV, additive residual error | n/a | Results paragraph after Figure 1 |
| Covariates CLCr (Cockcroft-Gault) on CL, Age on V1 | n/a | Results (forward inclusion / backward elimination); Table 2 |
| 1 g q12h by 1-hour infusion, age 50 years, CLCr 60/80/100 mL/min | n/a | Discussion and Figure 6 |

# Typical-value checks against the Discussion

The Discussion reports several typical values derived from the final model at
the modeling-group means (Table 1: CLCr 35.07 mL/min, age 66.62 years, weight
57.64 kg).

```{r typical-values}
th <- ui$theta
mean_crcl <- 35.07
mean_age <- 66.62
mean_wt <- 57.64

cl_typ <- exp(th[["lcl"]]) * mean_crcl
v1_typ <- exp(th[["lvc"]]) * mean_age
v2_typ <- exp(th[["lvp"]])

typical <- tibble::tribble(
  ~quantity, ~published, ~packaged,
  "CL at mean CLCr (L/h)", 1.56, cl_typ,
  "V1 (L/kg)", 0.63, v1_typ / mean_wt,
  "V2 (L/kg)", 0.77, v2_typ / mean_wt,
  "VDss = V1 + V2 (L/kg)", 1.39, (v1_typ + v2_typ) / mean_wt,
  "Residual SD / mean concentration 17.13 mg/L (%)", 26.32,
  100 * th[["addSd"]] / 17.13
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (packaged - published) / published)

typical |>
  mutate(packaged = signif(packaged, 4), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Quantity" = quantity,
    "Published (Discussion)" = published,
    "Packaged model" = packaged,
    "% difference" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical values quoted in the Discussion versus the packaged model at the Table 1 means.")

# These are pure arithmetic on the published estimates; the only source of
# disagreement is the rounding of theta1 to 0.044 in Table 2.
stopifnot(all(abs(typical$pct_diff) < 2))
```

The clearance at the mean CLCr is 1.54 L/h from the printed slope 0.044; the
Discussion's 1.56 L/h implies an unrounded slope of about 0.0445.

# Figure 6: simulated profiles in a 50-year-old patient

Figure 6 shows the concentration-time profile of 1 g every 12 hours (1-hour
infusion, read from the figure) in a 50-year-old patient with CLCr of 60, 80 and
100 mL/min. The figure has no legend in the published image; the lines are
assigned to CLCr by their order (dotted = 60, dashed = 80, solid = 100 mL/min),
since a lower CLCr gives higher concentrations. The points below were
digitised by the maintainers from Figure 6 at the start of the interval, at the
end of infusion, at 2 hours and at 12 hours.

The figure is labelled as steady state, but it matches the fifth dosing
interval (48-60 hours after the first dose) of the packaged model, not the
true steady state: at CLCr 60 mL/min the model is still accumulating at 60
hours (the trough rises from 17.7 to 19.3 mg/L across the interval, against
22.6 mg/L at true steady state). The simulation below shows both intervals.

```{r fig6-simulate}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

fig6_patients <- tibble::tibble(id = 1:3, CRCL = c(60, 80, 100), AGE = 50)

fig6_doses <- tidyr::crossing(fig6_patients, time = seq(0, 240, by = 12)) |>
  mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 1000, rate = 1000, cmt = "central")
fig6_obs <- tidyr::crossing(fig6_patients, time = seq(0, 252, by = 0.1)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_, cmt = "central")
fig6_events <- bind_rows(fig6_doses, fig6_obs) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()

fig6_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typ,
  events = fig6_events,
  keep = "CRCL",
  rtol = 1e-10,
  atol = 1e-12
) |>
  as.data.frame()

fig6_digitised <- tibble::tribble(
  ~CRCL, ~tad, ~Cc,
  60, 0, 19.2,
  60, 1, 48.3,
  60, 2, 37.6,
  60, 12, 19.3,
  80, 0, 13.3,
  80, 1, 43.4,
  80, 2, 33.3,
  80, 12, 13.7,
  100, 0, 10.0,
  100, 1, 40.0,
  100, 2, 30.0,
  100, 12, 10.3
)

fig6_intervals <- bind_rows(
  fig6_sim |>
    filter(time >= 48, time <= 60) |>
    mutate(tad = time - 48, interval = "5th dose (48-60 h)"),
  fig6_sim |>
    filter(time >= 228, time <= 240) |>
    mutate(tad = time - 228, interval = "Steady state (228-240 h)")
) |>
  mutate(CRCL = factor(CRCL))
```

```{r fig6-plot, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 6 of Purwonugroho 2012: 1 g every 12 hours by 1-hour infusion in a 50-year-old patient. Lines are the packaged model; points are digitised from the published figure."}
ggplot(fig6_intervals, aes(tad, Cc, colour = CRCL, linetype = interval)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(
    data = mutate(fig6_digitised, CRCL = factor(CRCL)),
    aes(tad, Cc, colour = CRCL),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 2
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 12, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)",
    y = "Vancomycin serum concentration (mg/L)",
    colour = "CLCr (mL/min)",
    linetype = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r fig6-compare}
fig6_check <- fig6_digitised |>
  mutate(time = 48 + tad) |>
  left_join(
    fig6_sim |>
      mutate(time = round(time, 1)) |>
      select(CRCL, time, Cc_sim = Cc),
    by = c("CRCL", "time")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (Cc_sim - Cc) / Cc)

fig6_check |>
  transmute(
    CRCL,
    tad,
    Cc,
    Cc_sim = round(Cc_sim, 1),
    pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "CLCr (mL/min)" = CRCL,
    "Time after dose (h)" = tad,
    "Figure 6 (mg/L)" = Cc,
    "Packaged, 5th dose (mg/L)" = Cc_sim,
    "% difference" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Figure 6 digitised values against the packaged typical-value model over the fifth dosing interval.")

# Deterministic typical-value comparison. The digitisation is read to about
# 0.5 mg/L; the pre-dose value of the dotted line is the hardest to read.
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(fig6_check$Cc_sim),
  abs(median(fig6_check$pct_diff)) < 3,
  all(abs(fig6_check$pct_diff[fig6_check$tad > 0]) < 6)
)
```

# Steady-state AUC: PKNCA against dose / CL

At true steady state the AUC over one dosing interval equals dose / CL. This
check runs PKNCA over the last simulated interval (228-240 hours) of the three
Figure 6 patients and compares it with `1000 mg / (0.044 * CLCr)`.

```{r pknca-ss}
ss_conc <- fig6_sim |>
  filter(time >= 228, time <= 240, !is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(time = time - 228, regimen = "1 g q12h") |>
  select(id, regimen, CRCL, time, Cc)

ss_dose <- fig6_patients |>
  mutate(time = 0, amt = 1000, regimen = "1 g q12h")

ss_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(ss_conc, Cc ~ time | regimen + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h"),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(ss_dose, amt ~ time | regimen + id, doseu = "mg"),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 12, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE)
))

ss_res <- as.data.frame(ss_nca$result) |>
  select(id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(fig6_patients, by = "id") |>
  mutate(
    auc_expected = 1000 / (exp(ui$theta[["lcl"]]) * CRCL),
    pct_diff = 100 * (auclast - auc_expected) / auc_expected
  )

ss_res |>
  transmute(
    CRCL,
    auc_expected = round(auc_expected, 1),
    auclast = round(auclast, 1),
    pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 2),
    cmax = round(cmax, 1),
    cmin = round(cmin, 1)
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "CLCr (mL/min)" = CRCL,
    "Dose / CL (mg*h/L)" = auc_expected,
    "PKNCA AUC0-12 (mg*h/L)" = auclast,
    "% difference" = pct_diff,
    "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax,
    "Cmin (mg/L)" = cmin
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Steady-state AUC over one 12-hour interval: PKNCA against dose / CL.")

# Same parameters on both sides; the residual is trapezoidal error on a
# 0.1-hour grid (measured below 0.1%).
stopifnot(all(abs(ss_res$pct_diff) < 1))
```

# Virtual cohort

The virtual cohort reproduces the modeling-group covariate distributions of
Table 1. Age is normal with the reported mean and SD, truncated to 19-95
years. Creatinine clearance is log-normal with the reported mean and SD
(35.07 +/- 29.83 mL/min), truncated to 5-150 mL/min. The Table 1 SD is close
to the mean, so the distribution is strongly right-skewed, and the truncation
removes much of its upper tail: the sampled SD is smaller than the Table 1 SD.
Every subject receives 1 g every 12 hours by 1-hour infusion for three days,
the regimen of Figure 6; it is not individualised to renal function, which is
why the exposure in the lowest renal band is high.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20120417)
set.seed(20120417)
n_sub <- 200L

rtrunc_norm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  x <- rnorm(n, mean, sd)
  while (any(out <- x < lo | x > hi)) x[out] <- rnorm(sum(out), mean, sd)
  x
}
rtrunc_lnorm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (sd / mean)^2))
  meanlog <- log(mean) - sdlog^2 / 2
  x <- rlnorm(n, meanlog, sdlog)
  while (any(out <- x < lo | x > hi)) x[out] <- rlnorm(sum(out), meanlog, sdlog)
  x
}

cohort <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  AGE = rtrunc_norm(n_sub, 66.62, 18.38, 19, 95),
  CRCL = rtrunc_lnorm(n_sub, 35.07, 29.83, 5, 150)
) |>
  mutate(
    renal_band = cut(
      CRCL,
      breaks = c(0, 30, 60, Inf),
      labels = c("CLCr < 30", "CLCr 30-60", "CLCr >= 60"),
      right = FALSE
    )
  )

cohort |>
  summarise(
    "Age mean (SD), years" = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(AGE), sd(AGE)),
    "CLCr mean (SD), mL/min" = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(CRCL), sd(CRCL)),
    "CLCr < 30 / 30-60 / >= 60 (n)" = paste(table(renal_band), collapse = " / ")
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Virtual cohort covariates (Table 1 modeling group: age 66.62 +/- 18.38 years; CLCr 35.07 +/- 29.83 mL/min).")
```

```{r cohort-simulate}
cohort_doses <- tidyr::crossing(cohort, time = seq(0, 60, by = 12)) |>
  mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 1000, rate = 1000, cmt = "central")
cohort_obs <- tidyr::crossing(cohort, time = seq(0, 72, by = 0.25)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_, cmt = "central")
cohort_events <- bind_rows(cohort_doses, cohort_obs) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()

cohort_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = cohort_events,
  keep = c("renal_band", "CRCL", "AGE")
) |>
  as.data.frame()
stopifnot(!anyNA(cohort_sim$Cc))
```

```{r vpc, fig.cap = "Simulated vancomycin concentrations (individual predictions without residual error) for 1 g every 12 hours in the virtual cohort, by renal-function band: median and 5th-95th percentiles. Dashed lines mark the 10-20 mg/L trough band discussed in the paper."}
cohort_sim |>
  group_by(renal_band, time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    p50 = median(Cc),
    p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(10, 20), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  facet_wrap(~renal_band) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 72, 12)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Vancomycin (mg/L)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# PKNCA over the first and fifth dosing intervals

The paper reports no NCA, so this section summarises the simulated exposure
over the first dose and over the fifth dose (the interval shown in Figure 6)
by renal-function band.

```{r pknca-cohort}
nca_conc <- cohort_sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, renal_band, time, Cc)

nca_dose <- cohort_doses |>
  select(id, renal_band, time, amt) |>
  as.data.frame()

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | renal_band + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h"),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | renal_band + id, doseu = "mg"),
  intervals = data.frame(
    start = c(0, 48),
    end = c(12, 60),
    cmax = TRUE,
    auclast = TRUE
  )
))

# The trough at the end of each interval is read straight from the
# simulation (the value just before the next dose).
troughs <- nca_conc |>
  filter(time %in% c(12, 60)) |>
  transmute(
    renal_band,
    id,
    start = time - 12,
    PPTESTCD = "trough",
    PPORRES = Cc
  )

nca_summary <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")) |>
  select(renal_band, id, start, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  bind_rows(troughs) |>
  mutate(interval = ifelse(start == 0, "Dose 1 (0-12 h)", "Dose 5 (48-60 h)")) |>
  group_by(renal_band, interval, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(
    value = sprintf(
      "%.1f [%.1f-%.1f]",
      median(PPORRES),
      quantile(PPORRES, 0.05),
      quantile(PPORRES, 0.95)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = value)

nca_summary |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Renal band" = renal_band,
    "Interval" = interval,
    "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax,
    "Trough at end of interval (mg/L)" = trough,
    "AUC0-12 (mg*h/L)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated NCA by renal-function band, median [5th-95th percentile].")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Interindividual variability.** The authors selected a "proportional"
  interindividual error model (`P_i = P_TV * (1 + eta)`) and report its
  magnitude as a percent CV, which for that model equals `sqrt(omega^2)`. The
  packaged model uses the exponential form `P_TV * exp(eta)` with
  `omega^2 = (CV/100)^2`, which is the same to first order and keeps every
  individual parameter positive. With the published 57.27% CV on V2, the
  proportional form would give a negative V2 in about 4% of simulated
  subjects.
* **Infusion duration.** The paper does not state the infusion duration of the
  clinical data. Figure 6 shows a 1-hour infusion, which is used throughout
  this article.
* **Figure 6 interval and legend.** The published figure has no legend, so the
  line styles were mapped to CLCr by concentration order. Although labelled as
  steady state, the figure agrees with the fifth dosing interval of the
  packaged model (within 2% at the peak and at 12 hours for all three
  patients) and not with true steady state, where the CLCr 60 mL/min trough is
  about 17% higher.
* **Covariate scale.** CLCr is the Cockcroft-Gault estimate in raw mL/min,
  stored in the `CRCL` column. CL and V1 are through-origin linear functions,
  so CL approaches zero as CLCr approaches zero and V1 is proportional to age;
  the model was built on patients with mean CLCr 35 mL/min (34% on dialysis)
  and mean age 67 years and should not be extrapolated far outside them.
* **Virtual cohort.** Table 1 gives only means and SDs. The log-normal shape of
  CLCr and the truncation limits for age and CLCr are assumptions.
* **Inconsistent precision figures.** The precision of the fixed effects in the
  Discussion (4.98%-28.34%) and of the omega estimates (V1 117.00%, Q
  158.00%, CL 22.9%, V2 67.68%) do not match the estimation errors printed in
  Table 2, and the abstract gives the RMSE as 12.2 mg/L against 12.28 mg/L in
  the Results. None of these affects the point estimates used here, which are
  taken from Table 2.
* **Errata.** No erratum or correction for this article was found on
  Europe PMC or PubMed (checked 2026-11-19).
